events.title: China Stock Market May Reclaim 3,900-Point Level
events.description: The China stock market has finished lower in back-to-back sessions, contracting more than 60 points or 1.5 percent in that span. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,890-point plateau although it's likely to open to the upside on Monday.

events.title: Taiwan Stock Market May Halt Its Slide On Monday
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has finished lower in two consecutive trading days, shedding almost 1,000 points or 2.2 percent along the way. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 46,180-point plateau although it's due for support on Monday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market May Extend Friday's Gains
events.description: The Singapore stock market on Friday ended the four-day losing streak in which it had retreated almost 110 points or 3.4 percent. The Straits Times Index now sits just beneath the 5,700-point plateau and it may add to its winnings on Monday.

events.title: Malaysia Stock Market Due For Support On Monday
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has finished lower in four sessions, slipping almost 30 points or 2 percent in that span. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just above the 1,685-point plateau although it may find traction on Monday.

events.title: Rebound Anticipated For Japan Stock Market
events.description: The Japan stock market headed south again on Friday, one day after ending the two-day slide in which it had stumbled more than 1,250 points or 1.9 percent. The Nikkei 225 now sits just above the 64,000-point plateau although it may bounce higher again on Monday.

events.title: South Korea Shares May Find Traction On Monday
events.description: The South Korea stock market has finished lower in two straight sessions, slumping almost 150 points or 2.1 percent in that span. The KOSPI now sits just above the 6,900-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Monday.

events.title: Hong Kong Production, PPI Data Due On Monday
events.description: Hong Kong will on Monday release Q2 figures for industrial production and producer prices, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Ticks Higher Amid Inflation Data Release, Expectations Of Reopening Of Strait Of Hormuz
events.description: The U.S. Dollar value inched higher as investors weighed today's inflation data that pushed the odds for a rate hike in the U.S. higher against reports of an upcoming meeting between the Gulf Cooperation Council nations and Iran to hasten the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: TSX Climbs On Tech Rally, Looks Set To End 6-day Losing Streak
events.description: The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 0.36% Friday to 35,634.50 as technology stocks surged 3.5%, contributing significantly to gains. Oil prices fell following International Energy Agency's downward global oil demand forecast revision.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Modestly Higher
events.description: The Switzerland stock market closed modestly higher on Friday, in line with markets across Europe, as a sharp drop in oil prices helped lift sentiment.

events.title: European Markets Rise As Oil Prices Fall On IEA Demand Cut
events.description: European markets gained ground Friday after the International Energy Agency cut its global oil demand forecast, sending Brent crude futures down 3.5% to $103.50. The IEA now projects world oil demand will drop 2.5 million barrels per day this year versus its prior estimate of 1.6 million bpd.

events.title: U.S. Consumer Sentiment Deteriorates Much More Than Expected In September
events.description: A report released by the University of Michigan on Friday showed consumer sentiment in the U.S. has deteriorated by much more than anticipated in the month of September. The University of Michigan said its consumer sentiment index slumped to 47.8 in September after tumbling to 51.7 in August. Economists had expected the index to edge down to 51.0.

events.title: CPSC Recalls: 2.3 Mln Candy Bottles, Motorcycles, Dressers, Dual Fuel Ranges, Fire Spray Canisters
events.description: The U.S. Consumer Product safety Commission or CPSC has announced various recalls including more than 2.3 million sour crush candy bottles, motorcycles, six-drawer dressers, dual fuel ranges, hair dryer brushes, and fire spray canisters, among others.
